rationale: B wins because it finds the cleaner fourth lane: "The system's two claims, outage backup and peak-rate arbitrage, are separate purchases with separate math" is an actual consumer-finance assignment, not launch confetti. A is strong, but its fourth angle, "A profitable charger maker bets on a capital-heavy market," collapses into its own warning: "a description, not a story." That is the smell of padding in an otherwise useful set.
gaps_in_A: A over-refuses the homeowner/payback lane: "Homeowners ride out blackouts on Anker's new battery" is rightly killed as a fake customer story, but the update does support a conditional consumer-finance angle around outage backup and peak-rate bills.
The fourth angle is undercooked: "Right now the facts support only 'large, profitable, publicly traded,' which is a description, not a story." Correct. So do not sell it as one of the four.

Some contextual color reaches past the supplied facts: "purchase costing thousands of dollars and living on the side of the house for a decade" and "an electrician's week" may be true-ish category assumptions, but they are not in the update.
The next step is too narrow: "journalist-fit-check on the Powerwall counterposition angle" skips the installer claim, which has the sharper falsifiable hook and needs less market-comparison data.
gaps_in_B: "category-creation" is a little inflated. The update supports Anker crossing categories; it does not prove "battery storage is becoming a consumer-electronics product" without broader market evidence.

The homeowner angle is mislabeled as "customer-story" while admitting it needs "at least one real US household using the system." Until that exists, it is a consumer-finance explainer, not a customer story.

"A competing product is actually on sale in the US, which is now" slightly overstates the facts. The update says Anker is launching in the US, not that units are installed, available nationwide, or actively selling.

The next step overreaches: "every one of them is a launch-day story with no current signal under it." The US launch itself is a legitimate peg for trade and business press; a newsjack hook would raise the ceiling, not become mandatory.
